To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fragments produced in the 84Kr+93 Nb reaction at 34 MeV/u have an almost constant speed corresponding to the speed of 80–90% of the projectile velocity.

(i) the angular distributions of the fragments are very narrow, (ii) the velocity of the fragments is almost independent of their charge, and (iii) the fragments are emitted in the forward direction with respect to the beam direction, which is in agreement with previous studies of the same reaction.
the fragments have a velocity close to that of the incident nucleus, and the fragments are emitted in the direction of the beam.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of high energy fragments in the84Kr + 93Nb reaction at an incident energy of 34.5MeV/u.
the study of the reaction mechanism of heavy ion collisions.
the study of the nuclear reaction mechanism in the84Kr +93Nb system at 34.53 MeV/u.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high-energy fragments are mainly emitted from a hot source moving with 0.8–0.9 of the velocity of the projectile.
the reaction mechanism in the84Kr +93Nb system at the highest energies studied is a mixture of deep inelastic scattering and fission.
a significant part of the detected fragments are produced in a process of the projectile fragmentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fragments are mainly produced by sequential binary decay of a heavy compound nucleus.
the fragments are emitted in a very fast way.
the fragments produced in the reaction have a large component of the projectile velocity and a large angular range, which is consistent with the picture of a deep inelastic process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the velocity of fragments with charge Z⩽Zp−2 (Zp is the projectile charge) is very close to that of the projectile, which indicates that they are emitted in a very fast process.
the high-energy fragments are not the result of the projectile fission.
the fragments with Z<30 are emitted at an angle of ∼4∘, while those with Z>30 are emitted isotropically.
